newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rabobank says to continue sale of Telekom options.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank says to continue sale of Telekom options.

text.p: The German unit of Dutch bank Rabobank said on Wednesday it would keep selling options on Deutsche Telekom stock, despite what it labelled "hindrance" from unidentified quarters.
Rabobank Germany chief executive officer Albert Sonntag told a news briefing that the bank would not withdraw the option issue because of the "clear interest" its customers had shown in them.

Co-operative bank Rabobank, which is not part of the consortium behind the Telekom sell-off on November 18, issued 12 million American-style call and put warrants on Telekom shares on Monday, which it said had sold "with great success."

But the bank said on Tuesday that within hours of the initial issue it received a series of requests to cancel the purchase of the options. It said this represented "unusual hindrance" of its ability to do business.

Rabobank said on Wednesday it had still not received any explanation from the banks why they had sought to cancel their purchase orders. The cancellation requests had all arrived at the same time and came mostly from banks within the Telekom syndicate, it added.
"We still have no clear explanation," Peter Geis, Rabobank's head of financial markets in Germany said.
A spokesman for Deutsche Telekom AG said it was making no comment on the Rabobank complaints.

Sonntag said that Rabobank had received cancellation requests for 50 percent of the options sold on Tuesday but would not fulfil the requests because it had not been given any plausible reason why it should do so.
Rabobank said that it was not accusing Deutsche Telekom directly or any particular banks in the syndicate for the cancellation of the option orders and said it would not be taking any legal action.
Sonntag said that there had been options issued on stock before previous flotations without any such difficulties.
Rabobank had since been flooded with calls from private customers interested in the options, whose own house banks refused to sell the paper to the private clients.

As Rabobank was not a member of the Telekom consortium it was under no obligation not to issue Telekom options during the current book-building phase, which goes on until the weekend after next, the board said.

On Friday, Deutsche Bank, one of the lead sponsors in the Telekom sell-off, issued options on Deutsche Telekom, which it later withdrew as it was told that the flotation contract prevented it from issuing such options.
